q.q: A square paper is folded in half twice to form a smaller square. If a notch is cut from the corner that corresponds to the center of the original square, what pattern is formed?
o: A square hole in the center
A diamond hole in the center
Four small squares at the corners
A cross shape in the center
q.x: The corner of the folded square that meets the center of the original sheet becomes the center when unfolded. Cutting a notch there results in a square hole at the exact center of the paper.

q.q: A circular paper is folded three times to form a sector of 45 degrees. A small circle is punched near the pointed center. How many holes will be visible after unfolding?
q.x: Folding a circle into 45-degree sectors implies 8 layers of paper. A hole punched at the apex of the sector will appear once at the center of the circle because all layers meet at that single point.

q.q: A square paper is folded along both diagonals and then a small semi-circle is cut along the hypotenuse edge. What will the pattern look like after unfolding?
q.x: The diagonal folds create four triangular sections. Cutting a semi-circle from the hypotenuse edge reflects across the folds. This results in four semi-circles positioned along the edges of the original square.

q.q: A square paper is folded vertically, then horizontally, then diagonally. A hole is punched at the center of the folded edge. How many holes will appear?
q.x: Folding a square three times creates 8 layers. A hole punched through the folded edge will penetrate all 8 layers, resulting in 8 holes when the paper is fully opened.

q.q: A square sheet is folded in half diagonally. A perpendicular cut is made from the folded edge towards the open edge. What is the result when unfolded?
o: A diamond shape in the center
q.x: A cut made perpendicular to the fold of a triangle results in a V-shape or an X-shape depending on the depth. When the triangle is unfolded, the symmetry creates two intersecting lines.

q.q: A square paper is folded into a smaller square, and a notch is cut out of the side that is not an edge of the original paper. How many cut-out shapes will appear on the final unfolded sheet?
q.x: Folding a square into a smaller square involves two folds, resulting in four layers. A cut made on the inner side (the fold) will be mirrored across the axis of the folds. Consequently, four notches will appear symmetrically on the original sheet.

q.q: A square paper is folded to form a smaller square. Two holes are punched in the center. How many holes are visible after unfolding?
q.x: A square folded into a smaller square has 4 layers. Punching 2 holes through 4 layers results in 8 holes total (2 holes * 4 layers = 8).

q.q: A triangular piece of paper is folded by bringing the apex to the midpoint of the base. A small triangle is then cut from the bottom-left corner of this folded shape. How many holes appear when the paper is unfolded?
q.x: Folding the apex to the base midpoint creates two layers of paper in the folded area. Cutting a corner from the folded shape will result in one hole in each of the two layers. Therefore, unfolding the paper reveals two triangular holes.

q.q: A rectangular sheet is folded twice horizontally. A punch is made at the center of the folded edge. How many holes are created?
q.x: Folding a rectangular sheet twice horizontally results in four layers. However, the punch is on the folded edge. Since the edge represents the fold line, each punch affects two layers simultaneously, resulting in two holes when opened.

q.q: A square sheet is folded into a smaller square. Two small squares are cut from the corners of the folded edge. How many holes are created when the paper is unfolded?
q.x: Folding a square into a smaller square creates 4 layers. Cutting 2 corners from the folded edges affects all layers. Each corner cut results in 2 holes, totaling 8 holes.

q.q: A square paper is folded along both diagonals. A cut is made at the center point where all folds meet. What is the result when unfolded?
o: A single hole in the center
A diamond shape in the center
Four small triangles at the center
A square hole in the center
q.x: When a square is folded along both diagonals, the center point of the paper becomes the common vertex of all four triangular layers. Cutting the corner of this vertex removes a small portion from each layer, which, when combined upon unfolding, creates a square hole.

q.q: A paper is folded twice to form a small square. Two small diamond-shaped cuts are made on the folded edges. How many diamond shapes will be seen on the unfolded paper?
q.x: Folding the paper twice creates four layers. Since two cuts are made on the folded edges (which involve multiple layers), each cut creates two holes per layer connection, totaling eight holes.

q.q: A triangular sheet is folded along its median. Then, a small triangle is cut out from the folded edge. When the sheet is unfolded, what is the resulting shape of the cutouts?
o: A single rhombus in the center
Two triangles joined at the base
q.x: Folding along the median and cutting the edge means the cut is reflected across the fold line. When unfolded, the two cutouts join at their bases to form a rhombus or two mirrored triangles depending on the angle. Given the options, two triangles joined at the base is the standard geometric result.

q.q: A square paper is folded along its vertical axis, then folded again along the horizontal axis. A circular hole is punched at the intersection of the two folds. How many holes appear when unfolded?
q.x: Because the punch is at the intersection point (the center of the paper), all four layers share the exact same location for the punch. Therefore, only one hole is created at the center of the unfolded sheet.

q.q: A rectangular paper is folded in half along the width, then folded in half again. A semicircular cut is made along the closed edge. What pattern is formed?
q.x: Folding the paper twice creates four layers. Cutting a semicircle along the closed edge means each layer provides a mirrored half-circle. Because there are two folds, this results in two complete circles appearing on the paper when unfolded.

q.q: A square paper is folded twice into a smaller square. Two parallel line cuts are made across the diagonal of the folded square. What is the pattern on the unfolded sheet?
o: Two large intersecting lines forming an 'X'
Four sets of parallel lines across the paper
A central square with two lines passing through
q.x: Two parallel cuts on a folded square produce four distinct sets of lines. Due to the reflection across the folds, these manifest as four sets of parallel lines mirrored across the four quadrants.

q.q: A paper is folded twice to form a square. A corner is cut off. How many corners will the resulting shape have?
q.x: Each fold adds complexity to the perimeter. Cutting a corner from a 4-layered folded square results in 8 corners after the paper is unfolded back to its original state.

q.q: A piece of paper is folded in half, and then in half again. A cut is made such that it removes the entire corner of the folded stack. When unfolded, what shape is formed in the center of the paper?
q.x: Removing the corner of a twice-folded square creates four mirrored cuts that combine to form a square in the center of the original sheet. Each fold reflects the cut to the adjacent quadrant.

q.q: A square sheet of paper is folded in half horizontally, then folded in half vertically, and finally, a small circular hole is punched through the center of the folded stack. When the paper is unfolded, how many holes will appear?
q.x: When the paper is folded twice, it creates four layers of paper. A single punch through the center of the folded stack pierces all four layers. Therefore, unfolding the paper reveals four holes positioned symmetrically.

q.q: A square sheet of paper is folded in half vertically, then in half horizontally. A small triangular hole is cut at the center of the folded edge. When the paper is unfolded, how many triangular holes will appear?
q.x: When folded twice, the paper has 4 layers. Cutting a hole at the folded edge creates one hole per layer as it unfolds. Thus, 4 triangular holes appear in total.

q.q: A strip of paper is folded in a zig-zag (accordion) pattern of 4 folds. A hole is punched through the entire stack. How many holes appear when the strip is fully opened?
q.x: A zig-zag fold of 4 creases creates 5 layers of paper. A hole punched through the entire stack will result in 5 holes when the strip is laid out flat.

q.q: A circular paper is folded in half, and then folded in half again. A 'V' shaped cut is made on the curved edge. How many 'V' shapes appear on the unfolded paper?
q.x: Folding a circle twice creates four layers. A cut on the curved edge is reflected across the fold lines, resulting in four V-shapes symmetrically placed around the perimeter.

q.q: A paper is folded into thirds vertically. Then a vertical line is cut through the middle of the folded stack. How many slits appear when opened?
q.x: Folding into thirds creates three layers. A vertical cut through the middle of the stack intersects the two inner folds. When unfolded, this results in two distinct slits.

q.q: A square sheet is folded along the horizontal axis, then folded in half vertically. If a 'V' shape is cut from the corner that contains all the folds, what is the result?
q.x: The corner containing the folds is the center of the original square. A 'V' cut reflected four times across the horizontal and vertical axes creates a cross-like or star-like pattern in the center of the sheet.

q.q: A circular paper is folded twice to form a quadrant. A small square notch is cut from the corner that represents the center of the original circle. How many square holes will be visible upon unfolding?
q.x: The corner representing the center of the circle is only one point in the original paper. Cutting a notch there creates a single square hole in the very center of the circular paper. Unfolding does not duplicate this central hole.

q.q: A paper is folded in half, then folded again. A semi-circle is cut along the closed folded edge. What is the resulting shape after unfolding?
o: A full circle in the center
q.x: Cutting a semi-circle on a folded edge completes the circle when the paper is mirrored upon unfolding. Because it was folded twice, the mirror image creates one full circular hole in the center.

q.q: If a square paper is folded three times into a triangle and a small dot is marked on the middle of the folded side, how many dots will be seen upon unfolding?
q.x: Three folds create 8 layers. However, since the mark is on the fold, it is shared between adjacent layers. This results in 4 dots distributed symmetrically.

q.q: A rectangular sheet is folded in half three times (all folds parallel). A hole is punched in the center. How many holes appear?
q.x: Folding a sheet in half 3 times results in 8 layers (2^3). A punch through the center of 8 layers creates 8 holes in the final unfolded sheet.

q.q: Consider a square paper folded once to form a rectangle. If a 'V' shape is cut from the folded edge, what pattern appears upon unfolding?
o: Two 'V' shapes pointing in the same direction
q.x: A 'V' cut on the folded edge reflects to create a diamond shape when the paper is unfolded. The point of the 'V' becomes the center of the diamond.

q.q: A circular paper is folded twice to form a quadrant. A small 'V' shape is cut along the curved edge of the quadrant. How many 'V' shapes will be visible after unfolding the paper completely?
q.x: Folding a circle into a quadrant creates 4 layers. Because the 'V' is cut on the curved edge (the outer perimeter), unfolding it results in 2 'V' shapes, as the cut is shared across the fold line.

q.q: A square paper is folded to form a triangle. Two small circular holes are punched on the triangle. How many holes are visible after unfolding?
q.x: Folding a square into a triangle creates two layers. Punching two holes through two layers results in 2 x 2 = 4 holes upon unfolding.

q.q: A rectangular paper is folded twice along the length, and then a V-shaped cut is made on the folded edge. When unfolded, what is the appearance of the cut?
q.x: A V-shaped cut on a folded edge acts as a mirror image when unfolded. Because the paper was folded twice, the mirror effect repeats, turning the V-shape into a complete diamond or rhombus shape in the center of the sheet.

q.q: A rectangular paper is folded twice such that it becomes a long strip. A hole is punched through the center. How many holes are seen when the strip is unfolded?
q.x: Folding a rectangle into a strip typically involves two folds creating four layers. A single punch through the center of these four layers will result in four distinct holes when the paper is completely unfolded.

q.q: A square paper is folded along both diagonals to form a small triangle. A corner cut is made at the tip (the common vertex). When unfolded, what shape is visible in the center?
q.x: The tip of the triangle formed by folding along both diagonals corresponds to the center of the square. Cutting this tip creates a hole that expands into a square when the paper is unfolded.

q.q: A piece of paper is folded vertically twice. A hole is punched in the bottom left corner of the final folded rectangle. Where will the holes appear?
o: At the four corners of the original sheet
At the bottom two corners only
At the left edge of the paper
q.x: Folding twice vertically creates four layers. The bottom left corner of the folded stack represents the four corners of the original rectangle. Therefore, punching that corner results in four holes, one at each corner of the original sheet.

q.q: A square paper is folded in half, then a small triangle is cut from the folded side. How many triangles are visible when unfolded?
q.x: Folding a square in half creates two layers. A cut on the fold line creates a mirror image of the triangle, resulting in two triangles joined at the base when opened.

q.q: A rectangular paper is folded twice along its length. A circular punch is made in the center of the folded strip. How many circles will appear when the paper is unfolded?
q.x: Folding a paper in half twice creates 4 layers. A punch made in the center of the folded strip goes through all 4 layers. Therefore, 4 circles will appear symmetrically.

q.q: Consider a paper folded into four equal squares. A small hole is punched in the center of one of the outer squares. How many holes will be visible when the paper is unfolded?
q.x: Since the hole is punched in only one of the four folded squares (and not along any of the fold lines), that hole exists only on that specific layer. Unfolding the paper reveals only that single hole.

q.q: A triangular paper is folded in half once. A rectangular slit is cut on the folded edge. How many slits appear when unfolded?
q.x: Folding a triangle in half creates 2 layers. A slit cut on the folded edge results in two halves of the slit merging into one, but because it is on the fold, it produces two distinct slits when unfolded.

q.q: A circular paper is folded thrice to form a wedge shape (1/8th of a circle). A semi-circular cut is made on the curved edge. When unfolded, what will be the result?
o: Eight circular holes along the outer edge
Four large semi-circular cutouts on the perimeter
Eight semi-circular indents along the edge
A flower pattern with eight petals
q.x: Since the paper is folded into 1/8th of a circle, the cut on the curved edge will be reflected 8 times. A semi-circular cut on the folded edge results in eight semi-circular indents along the perimeter of the circle.

q.q: A rectangular paper is folded three times: once horizontally, once vertically, and once diagonally. A circular hole is punched through the folded corner. How many holes appear in total?
q.x: Folding three times results in 2^3 = 8 layers of paper. Punching a hole through the corner of this folded stack creates 8 holes when unfolded. Each layer contributes one hole to the final pattern.

q.q: A circular paper is folded in half twice. A small circle is cut from the outer curved edge. How many circles will be visible upon unfolding?
q.x: The circular paper folded twice results in four layers. Cutting the outer edge creates one hole per layer. Therefore, four circles will be visible, arranged symmetrically along the outer perimeter.

q.q: A square paper is folded along both diagonals to form a smaller triangle. A corner is then cut off from the folded tip. When unfolded, which shape is formed in the middle?
q.x: Folding a square into a triangle by diagonals results in four layers meeting at the center. Cutting the tip removes the central point, creating a square hole when unfolded.

q.q: A rectangular paper is folded into thirds. A hole is punched through all three layers. How many holes appear in total?
q.x: Folding a sheet into three layers creates a stack of three papers. A single punch through all layers will result in three distinct holes when the sheet is opened.

q.q: A square paper is folded along both diagonals to form a small triangle. A hole is punched at the tip of the triangle (the center of the original square). How many holes appear upon unfolding?
q.x: The tip of the triangle corresponds to the center of the square. Since all folds converge at this single point, punching it only creates one single hole at the center of the unfolded square.

q.q: A paper in the shape of an equilateral triangle is folded by bringing the three corners to the center. What is the resulting shape before any cutting?
q.x: Folding the corners of an equilateral triangle to the center point results in a smaller equilateral triangle that is exactly half the side length of the original. This is a standard geometric fold pattern.

q.q: If a rectangular paper is folded vertically and then punched with a diamond-shaped hole at the fold, what is the resulting shape when unfolded?
q.x: Because the punch is made exactly on the fold line, the diamond is cut in half. When the paper is unfolded, the two halves join to form one single, complete diamond shape.

q.q: A rectangular paper is folded once horizontally and then a circular punch is made in the bottom right corner. If unfolded, where will the holes appear?
q.x: Folding horizontally means the bottom half is behind the top half. A punch in the bottom right corner of the folded stack creates a hole in the bottom right of the bottom half and the bottom right of the top half (which is the top right when looking at the full sheet).

q.q: If you fold a paper in half vertically and then punch two holes in the folded edge, how many holes will you see when you unfold the paper?
q.x: Folding once creates two layers. Punching the folded edge creates holes in both layers at the same spot. Since the holes are on the fold line, they remain as two distinct holes upon unfolding.

q.q: A square sheet of paper is folded in half vertically, then in half horizontally. A small triangular hole is cut at the center of the folded edge. How will the paper look when unfolded?
o: Four triangles forming a diamond shape in the center
Two triangles at the top and two at the bottom
Four triangles pointing outward from the center
A large diamond in the center with four small holes
q.x: When the paper is folded twice, the center of the folded edges represents the middle of each side of the square. A cut at the center of the folded edge creates four symmetrical shapes meeting at the center of the square. These form a diamond shape when unfolded.

q.q: A circular paper is folded in half. A small square punch is made on the straight folded diameter. When unfolded, what is the result?
q.x: A square cut along the folded diameter of a circle creates two identical squares that are adjacent to each other at the center of the circle when unfolded.

q.q: A circular paper is folded in half three times to form a sector. A small punch is made near the pointed center. How many holes are visible upon unfolding?
q.x: Folding a circle in half three times creates 8 layers of paper. A single punch through 8 layers creates 8 distinct holes when the paper is fully opened. The holes will be arranged in a circle around the center point.

q.q: A square sheet of paper is folded in half vertically, then folded in half again horizontally. A small triangular hole is punched at the center of the folded edge. When the paper is unfolded, how many triangular holes will appear in total?
q.x: The paper is folded into four quadrants. Punching a hole on the center of the folded edge means the hole intersects the fold line between two quadrants. Unfolding results in two holes symmetric across the fold line.

q.q: A rectangular sheet is folded in half along its length, and then a semi-circular cut is made on the folded edge. How does the unfolded paper appear?
o: A full circle in the center
One large semi-circle on the edge
q.x: Cutting a semi-circle on the fold of a doubled paper creates two mirror-image semi-circles joined at the diameter. When unfolded, these two halves align to form a complete circle in the center of the sheet.

q.q: A square paper is folded diagonally twice. A triangle is cut from the folded side that is not the center point. What is the final appearance?
o: One large triangle in the center
q.x: Folding diagonally twice creates four layers. Cutting a triangle from the edge reflects that cut into each of the four outer edges of the square. Thus, four triangles appear near the edges.

q.q: If a paper is folded horizontally and then vertically, and a square is cut out from the corner that contains the folded center, what does the paper look like unfolded?
o: One square at each of the four sides
q.x: Cutting the center corner of a folded square removes the point where all four quadrants meet. Unfolding this creates a single square hole exactly in the middle of the paper.

q.q: A square sheet of paper is folded in half horizontally, then folded in half vertically, and finally, a small circular hole is punched through the center of the folded stack. When unfolded, what will the pattern look like?
o: A single circle in the center
Four circles arranged in a square pattern
A large circle made of four arcs
q.x: Since the paper was folded twice (creating four layers), a single punch through the center of the folded stack results in four symmetric holes. When unfolded, these holes are positioned at the center of each of the four quadrants created by the folds. Thus, they appear as four circles arranged in a square.

q.q: A triangular paper is folded from the top vertex to the base. A small hole is punched in the middle of the new base. How many holes are seen when unfolded?
q.x: The fold creates two layers. A hole punched through the base of the folded triangle passes through both layers, resulting in two holes symmetrically located on the original triangle.

q.q: A circular paper is folded in half three times. A triangular cut is made at the center point. How many triangles are visible when unfolded?
q.x: Folding a circle in half three times creates 8 sectors. A cut at the center point passes through all 8 layers, resulting in 8 triangular holes arranged in a radial pattern.

q.q: A square sheet is folded into a smaller square. Two small circles are punched near the closed corner. How many circles will appear on the paper after unfolding?
q.x: Folding a square into a smaller square creates 4 layers. Punching two holes through 4 layers results in 2 * 4 = 8 total holes. The holes will be symmetrically distributed around the center of the sheet.
